register.name: PCI_DMA_CTRL_DATA_ARB_PRIOR_OFF
register.comment: DMA Arbitration Scheme for TRGT1 Interface. This register is used to control traffic priorities among various sources that are delivered to your application through TRGT1 where 0x0 represents the highest priority. - Non-DMA Rx Requests - DMA Write Channel MRd Requests (DMA data requests and LL element/descriptor access) - DMA Read Channel MRd Requests (LL element/descriptor access) - DMA Read Channel MWr Requests Concurrent traffic from channels with same priority are sorted according to Round-Robin arbitration rules. The arbitration priority defaults to Non-DMA requests (highest), Write Channel MRd, Read Channel MRd, Read Channel MWr. For more information, see the 'Internal Architecture' section in the DMA chapter of the Databook.

register.name: PCI_DMA_CTRL_OFF
register.comment: DMA Number of Channels Register. This register provides information regarding the number of configured DMA read and write channels. Note: When this register does not exist, value is fixed to 32'hFFFF_FFFF.

register.name: PCI_DMA_WRITE_ENGINE_EN_OFF
register.comment: DMA Write Engine Enable Register. This register indicates the status of DMA write engine and the status of DMA write engine handshake feature (per-channel).

register.name: PCI_DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF
register.comment: DMA Write Doorbell Register. This register controls the DMA write channel doorbell.

register.name: PCI_DMA_WRITE_ENGINE_PF_OFF
register.comment: DMA Write Engine Pre-Fetch Register. This is the DMA write engine pre-fetch register.

register.name: PCI_DMA_READ_ENGINE_EN_OFF

register.name: PCI_DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF

register.name: PCI_DMA_READ_ENGINE_PF_OFF

register.name: PCI_DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF

register.name: PCI_DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF

register.name: PCI_DMA_WRITE_LINKED_LIST_ERR_EN_OFF
register.comment: DMA Write Linked List Error Enable Register. The LIE and RIE bits in the LL element enable the channel 'done' interrupts (local and remote). The LLLAIE and LLRAIE bits enable the channel 'abort' interrupts (local and remote).
